html:
The Taliban are a Sunni Islamist movement that ruled most of Afghanistan from 1996 to 2001 and has ruled the whole country again since August 2021. Their name means "students".

They grew out of the chaos that followed the Soviet war and the civil war among the mujahideen. Many leaders had studied in Deobandi religious schools among Afghan refugees in Pakistan. Led by Mullah Mohammed Omar, they appeared around Kandahar in 1994, promised order, and took Kabul in 1996. Their main enemy in the north was Ahmad Shah Massoud.

Their first government enforced a harsh reading of Islamic law. Women were kept from school and most work, music and television were banned, and in 2001 they blew up the Buddhas of Bamiyan. They also hosted Osama bin Laden and al-Qaeda. After the attacks of 11 September 2001, a US-led invasion drove them from power.

They fought a long insurgency from bases in Afghanistan and Pakistan. After the United States agreed to leave, they took Kabul in August 2021, as the Kabul airlift carried thousands of Afghans out. Since then they have again barred girls from secondary school and banned opium growing.
sum: The Taliban are a Sunni Islamist movement that ruled most of Afghanistan from 1996 to 2001 and has ruled the whole country again since August 2021. Their name means "students".
